newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kansai Elec Y2 trln power plant plan gets go sign.
newsitem.headline: Kansai Elec Y2 trln power plant plan gets go sign.

text.p: The Wakayama prefectural government in central Japan said on Thursday it had approved Kansai Electric Power Co Inc's two trillion yen plan to build two power plants in the area.
"We informed the (government's) Economic Planning Agency of the governor's approval on Wednesday," an official for the prefectural government said.

A government electricity panel is expected to approve Kansai Electric's plan later this month, which will then effectively become part of Japan's official long term power supply programme, a trade ministry official said.
Kansai Electric plans to build a 4.4 million kilowatt (kw) power plant in Gobo on the Pacific coast, and a 3.7 million kw plant in Wakayama city, 60 km southwest of Osaka.
The power plant in Gobo, to consist of four generators which will mainly run on orimulsion, will start commercial operations January 2007, a Kansai Electric spokesman said.
Orimulsion is a tar-like fuel made up of water and bitumen.
The plant in Wakayama city will use natural gas as fuel, and the first of the five generators, each with capacity of 740,000 kw, is scheduled to begin commercial operations in November 2004, he said.
With the added capacity from the new plants, Kansai Electric is expected to be able to meet the region's growing power demand until about 2015, he added.
